children: US equity futures traded lower ahead of Nvidia's earnings report due out on Tuesday and the planned stock market debut of AI firm Anthropic later this week.

Nvidia remained under pressure following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman alleged to have links to Chinese intelligence, which sparked corporate governance and national security concerns.
In South Korea, the Kospi fell 3.6%, dragged down by heavyweight chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.

Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 2.25% after data showed the country's economy contracted in the latest quarter. AI-related stocks were among the biggest decliners, with SoftBank Group, Kioxia Holdings Tokyo Electron all falling.
Taiwan's Taiex shed 6%, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co dropping 5.7%.
Market sentiment was also weighed down by concerns that growth in AI-related capital spending could slow, adding to uncertainty surrounding the sector's outlook.

Elsewhere, Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 0.42%, while China's Shanghai Composite fell 0.87% after weaker-than-expected economic data with industrial output growth slowing to 4.8% year-on-year in October from 5.5% in September while retail sales rose 0.4%, down from 1.1% a month earlier and below expectations.
Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in the first 10 months of the year, adding to concerns over the strength of the country's economic recovery and domestic demand.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 edged 0.4% lower, while India's Sensex gained 0.56%.
Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com
